explanation.text: The Louisiana Purchase treaty was signed in Paris, France, on April 30, 1803, as confirmed by the historical record from the National Archives and Wikipedia.
The treaty priced the territory at $15 million, not $10 million, according to the National Archives' transcription of the treaty and financial conventions.
This $15 million amount included $11,250,000 for the territory and $3,750,000 to settle American claims against France, as specified in the treaty conventions.
Wikipedia corroborates the $15 million figure, noting it was the agreed price after negotiations reduced the initial French asking price.
The claim that the territory was priced at $10 million is contradicted by both primary treaty documents and secondary historical synthesis.
The preliminary decision of 'false' is supported because the asserted price of $10 million does not match the documented $15 million total from the treaty.

excerpts.text: On April 11, 1803, just days before Monroe's arrival, Barbé-Marbois offered Livingston all of Louisiana for $15 million,[[18]](#cite_note-20) which averages to less than three cents per acre (7¢/ha).[[19]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurgan200236-21)[[20]](#cite_note-22) The total of $15 million is equivalent to about $380 million in 2024 dollars, or 72 cents per acre.

The Americans thought that Napoleon might withdraw the offer at any time, preventing the United States from acquiring New Orleans, so they agreed and signed the Louisiana Purchase Treaty on April 30, 1803 (10 Floréal XI in the [French Republican calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Republican_calendar "French Republican calendar")) at the [Hôtel Tubeuf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hôtel_Tubeuf "Hôtel Tubeuf") in Paris.[[22]](#cite_note-24) The signers were [Robert Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_R._Livingston_(chancellor) "Robert R.

[Francis Baring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Francis_Baring,_1st_Baronet "Sir Francis Baring, 1st Baronet")'s son [Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Baring,_1st_Baron_Ashburton "Alexander Baring, 1st Baron Ashburton") and Pierre Labouchère from Hopes arrived in Paris in April 1803 to assist with the negotiations.[[51]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZiegler198870-53)[[49]](#cite_note-Barings-51) With the bankers' help, the French and American negotiators settled on a price of 80 million francs ($15 million), down from an initial price of 100 million francs, a sum the Americans could not afford and the financers could not provide.[[49]](#cite_note-Barings-51) In the final agreement, the value of the U.S. currency was set at ⁠5+3333/10000⁠ francs per U.S. dollar.[[52]](#cite_note-54) In 2024 dollars, the $15 million purchase price is equivalent to about $380 million.

excerpts.text: **In this transaction with France, signed on April 30, 1803, the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million. For roughly 4 cents an acre, the United States doubled its size, expanding the nation westward.**

However, when they were offered the entire territory of Louisiana – an area larger than Great Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal combined – the American negotiators swiftly agreed to a price of $15 million.

*Note: The three documents transcribed here are the treaty of cession and two conventions, one for the payment of 60 million francs ($11,250,000), the other for claims American citizens had made against France for 20 million francs ($3,750,000).*

For the payment of the Sum of Sixty millions of francs mentioned in the preceeding article the United States shall create a Stock of eleven millions, two hundred and fifty thousand Dollars bearing an interest of Six percent per annum payable half yearly in London Amsterdam or Paris amounting by the half year to three hundred and thirty Seven thousand five hundred Dollars, according to the proportions which Shall be determined by the french Govenment to be paid at either place: The principal of the Said Stock to be reimbursed at the treasury of the United States in annual payments of not less than three millions of Dollars each; of which the first payment Shall commence fifteen years after the date of the exchange of ratifications:--this Stock Shall be transferred to the government of France or to Such person or persons as Shall be authorized to receive it in three months at most after the exchange of ratifications of this treaty and after Louisiana Shall be taken possession of the name of the Government of the United States.

The principal and interests of the Said debts Shall be discharged by the United States, by orders drawn by their Minister Plenipotentiary on their treasury, these orders Shall be payable Sixty days after the exchange of ratifications of the Treaty and the Conventions Signed this day, and after possession Shall be given of Louisiana by the Commissaries of France to those of the United States.
